ESTJ>INTJ.title: Someone who plans this week with next year in mind.
ESTJ>INTJ.body: You get today's work done quickly and plan ahead with the future in mind. You decide with logic and stick to a plan. Some days you lead discussions in front of everyone, and some days you want to think quietly alone. Before a meeting, you might go somewhere quiet to sort out your thoughts.
ESTJ>INTJ.do: On your lunch break, you read the news alone and think about next year's plans.
ESTJ>INTJ.worry: On days you lead in front of people, you want more alone time than you expected. It takes you a while to choose between the reliable way and a new way with the future in mind.
ESTJ>INTJ.karai: When someone says "Anywhere's fine," you pick a place in five minutes and even make the reservation.
ESTJ>INTJ.aru: You get this week's tasks done quickly, while in the back of your mind you're thinking, "Where will this be in three years?"
ESTJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people and trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone and follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with logic and stick to a plan. That's why, even while planning this week, you're thinking about what's ahead.
ESTJ>INTJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your getting-people-moving self or your thinking-ahead-alone self.
ESTJ>INTJ.plus: It takes you a while to decide because you're carefully comparing now and later. Later on, people often say what you decided was the right call.
ESTJ>INTJ.tip: On days you have something big to decide, take 30 minutes in the morning to think alone. You'll be able to speak up without hesitating in the afternoon discussion.
ESTJ>INTJ.hidden: When talking in a group, do you naturally ask, "So, who's doing what?" That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and you can move forward with others on what you thought through alone.

ESTJ>INTP.title: Someone who quickly asks, "Why is that?"
ESTJ>INTP.body: You don't just take what you're told as it is. You wonder, "Why?" When deciding something, you think it through with logic. At work you follow the set steps, but you're always wondering whether there's a better way. Even when watching the news, you look things up yourself, thinking, "Is that true?"
ESTJ>INTP.say: "Can you explain why it works that way?"
ESTJ>INTP.do: You compare phone plans from different companies and switch to a cheaper one.
ESTJ>INTP.worry: You want to follow the set way, but you also want to try your own way, and it leaves you uneasy. When you've been talking with people day after day, you want time to think alone.
ESTJ>INTP.karai: When a family member starts with "Probably...," you can't help asking, "Where'd you hear that?"
ESTJ>INTP.aru: You do your work by the manual, but inside you keep thinking, "Wouldn't it be faster to do these steps the other way around?"
ESTJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone, follow your ideas, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with logic. That's why "Why?" pops up even while you're following the rules.
ESTJ>INTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your following-the-steps-at-work self or your researching-alone-on-a-day-off self can give totally different results.
ESTJ>INTP.plus: You feel uneasy because you notice better ways. When someone asks for the reasons, the people around them make fewer mistakes.
ESTJ>INTP.tip: When a step bugs you, don't change it on the spot. Bring it up once: "This might be faster." If it's a good idea, others will start using it too.
ESTJ>INTP.hidden: In discussions, do you end up deciding, "So, by when will we do it?" That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can actually put your ideas into action.

ESTJ>ENTJ.title: Someone who comes up with new ideas based on last year's way.
ESTJ>ENTJ.body: You check how things have been done before, then think of something new. You work with people, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. At work, the one who looks at last year's way and says, "Let's change this part this year," is usually you.
ESTJ>ENTJ.say: "I've seen last year's numbers. Let's try a different way this year."
ESTJ>ENTJ.do: As the year-end party organizer, you keep the usual flow and add one new act.
ESTJ>ENTJ.worry: Sometimes you can't decide whether to go the usual way or try something new. You want to act with the future in mind, so it's frustrating when people say things are fine as they are.
ESTJ>ENTJ.karai: By the time you call a meeting to discuss it, the conclusion is already decided.
ESTJ>ENTJ.aru: When planning a trip, you make sure to hit the classic sights. Then you want to add just one "place hardly anyone goes."
ESTJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. That's why, when you look at last year's way, you want to add something new.
ESTJ>ENTJ.yure: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. Picture your daily work and you lean toward facts. Picture next year's plans and you lean toward ideas.
ESTJ>ENTJ.plus: It's frustrating because you can see what's ahead clearly. A new idea from someone who respects the usual way is easier for everyone to accept.
ESTJ>ENTJ.tip: When you share a new idea, say what you'll keep too: "Let's keep this from last year and change just this part." People feel at ease, and things move faster.
ESTJ>ENTJ.hidden: Do you first check, "How was it done before?" That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Because of it, people feel your new ideas are doable.

ESTJ>ENTP.title: Someone who throws out ideas and decides who's in charge on the spot.
ESTJ>ENTP.body: You keep throwing out ideas and move the conversation forward on the spot. Talking with people gives you energy, and you decide with logic. Sometimes you want to change what was decided, but in the end you see it through. Even on a trip with friends, you're the one who finally says, "Okay, let's go with this."
ESTJ>ENTP.say: "Good idea! Let's set the budget and deadline right now."
ESTJ>ENTP.do: After pitching lots of ideas in a planning meeting, you pick one at the end and decide who's in charge.
ESTJ>ENTP.worry: After deciding, you think of a better idea and want to change it. Sometimes you worry you're jerking people around.
ESTJ>ENTP.karai: When you lose a game, you say "One more time!" and won't quit.
ESTJ>ENTP.aru: You agreed to organize the party and even made the reservation, but on the day you want to switch: "Actually, that other place looks better."
ESTJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people and decide with logic. That's why new ideas come to you even after a decision is made.
ESTJ>ENTP.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture work plans and your result comes out structured. Picture plans with friends and it comes out freer.
ESTJ>ENTP.plus: You want to change things because you want to make them better. With someone who has lots of ideas and decides fast, conversations move quickly.
ESTJ>ENTP.tip: When you want to change a decision, set a rule: "Changes only up to the day before." It'll be easier for everyone to plan.
ESTJ>ENTP.hidden: Do you remember your go-to places and the ways that worked before? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can move new ideas forward in a way that works.

ESTJ>INFJ.title: Someone who keeps things on track and checks on anyone who seems down.
ESTJ>INFJ.body: You keep work on track, and you also watch how the people around you are doing. You set plans early and stick to them. You think about people's feelings and choose your words. After a meeting, you might ask someone who didn't say much, "What did you think back there?"
ESTJ>INFJ.do: While checking on work, you send a "You okay?" message only to the person who seems down.
ESTJ>INFJ.worry: Being with everyone is fun, but you feel wiped out after you get home. Sometimes you can't decide whether to say what's right or stay quiet for the other person's sake.
ESTJ>INFJ.karai: Even for plans to hang out, you're always the one who sends a reminder about the meeting time the day before.
ESTJ>INFJ.aru: The after-party is fun and you stay till the end, but the moment you get on the train home, you don't want to say a single word.
ESTJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone, follow your ideas, and decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you stick to a plan. That's why, even while moving fast, you notice how people are doing.
ESTJ>INFJ.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your busy-at-work self or your thinking-alone-at-home self can give totally different results.
ESTJ>INFJ.plus: You hesitate because you care about the other person's feelings. Someone who's organized and notices how people are doing is someone others rely on at work.
ESTJ>INFJ.tip: On party days, put in your earphones on the train home and listen to your favorite music. Making alone time keeps the tiredness from sticking around the next day.
ESTJ>INFJ.hidden: Do you remember how things went before, like "Last time it was like this"? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can give people concrete answers when they come to you for advice.

ESTJ>INFP.title: Someone who sets deadlines for the things they love.
ESTJ>INFP.body: You take the things you love and want to try seriously, and you set deadlines for them. In this combination, all four parts of your temperament and personality are flipped. Some days you need time alone with what you love, and some days you want to get things done with people. If you paint on weekends, you might have decided, "I'll finish one this month."
ESTJ>INFP.say: "This is going to be great. Let's finish it together."
ESTJ>INFP.do: You started a hobby just because you liked it, and now you've set monthly goals and you're taking it seriously.
ESTJ>INFP.worry: Even with something you love, setting a deadline can suddenly make it feel hard. You want to follow your feelings, but you end up thinking about whether it's right.
ESTJ>INFP.karai: When the talk turns to your favorite singer, you talk faster than usual.
ESTJ>INFP.aru: You were telling a friend about your dream, and before you know it you've set your own deadline: "Okay, let's get this far by Friday."
ESTJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone, follow your ideas, decide with your feelings, and go with the flow. All four parts are flipped in this combination. That's why you want to set deadlines even for what you love.
ESTJ>INFP.yure: All four parts are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Answering as your busy-at-work self or your doing-what-you-love-on-a-day-off self could give opposite results.
ESTJ>INFP.plus: It feels hard because you really care about what you love. Not many people see the things they love through to the end.
ESTJ>INFP.tip: For the things you love, try a loose deadline like "sometime this month." You can keep going while still having fun.
ESTJ>INFP.hidden: When you start something, do you naturally decide "what to do by when"? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, your dreams don't stay just talk.

ESTJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who sets up the practice schedule and praises everyone.
ESTJ>ENFJ.body: When doing something as a group, you set up the plan and keep things moving while praising each person. Being with people gives you energy, and you set plans early. You think about people's feelings and choose your words. Even at relay practice for a sports day, you might tell a slower kid, "You got faster than before."
ESTJ>ENFJ.say: "Your explanation just now was really easy to follow."
ESTJ>ENFJ.do: You agreed to put together the performance for a friend's wedding, and you set everyone's practice days.
ESTJ>ENFJ.worry: Even when there's something you want to point out, you think about the other person's feelings and can't say it. Trying to pull everyone's opinions together, you sometimes put your own last.
ESTJ>ENFJ.karai: You say, "I want to hear everyone's opinions," but you've already decided how the talk will end.
ESTJ>ENFJ.aru: Even when you want to point something out to a younger coworker, you keep thinking, "How can I say it without hurting them?" and the day ends.
ESTJ>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people and stick to a plan. That's why, even while setting up the plan, you think about how everyone feels.
ESTJ>ENFJ.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work plans and you lean toward facts and logic. Picture cheering on your teammates and you lean toward ideas and feelings.
ESTJ>ENFJ.plus: You can't say it because you care about the person. When advice comes from someone who praises them, people take it well.
ESTJ>ENFJ.tip: When you want to point something out, first mention one good thing, then say, "Let's fix just this part." You won't spend the whole day unsure.
ESTJ>ENFJ.hidden: Do you remember the ways that worked before, like "Last time we did it this way"? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can give concrete advice, not just encouragement.

ESTJ>ENFP.title: Someone who's always making plans for everyone to hang out.
ESTJ>ENFP.body: You like being with people and are always making plans for everyone to hang out. You value going with the moment, but you also end up thinking about the plan. You think about people's feelings so everyone can have fun. At a barbecue, you might be lighting the grill while checking that everyone has a drink.
ESTJ>ENFP.say: "I'll gather today's photos and send them to everyone later!"
ESTJ>ENFP.do: You make the group chat for hanging out, and you handle picking the date and checking who's coming yourself.
ESTJ>ENFP.worry: You want to spend time freely, but doing nothing makes you restless. Some days you worry so much about whether everyone's having fun that you don't enjoy yourself.
ESTJ>ENFP.karai: You say, "Let's go with no plan," but you've already looked up three places you want to go.
ESTJ>ENFP.aru: You decided to spend your day off freely, but by evening you feel a little down: "I didn't do anything."
ESTJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas, decide with your feelings, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people. That's why, even while having fun on a whim, you think about the plan.
ESTJ>ENFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your planning-at-work self or your hanging-out-with-friends self can give totally different results.
ESTJ>ENFP.plus: Doing nothing makes you restless because you want to enjoy each day. With someone who makes plans for everyone, get-togethers keep happening.
ESTJ>ENFP.tip: On a free day, add just one small plan, like "take a walk in the afternoon." You won't feel down by evening.
ESTJ>ENFP.hidden: When deciding something, do you compare, "Which is cheaper? Which is faster?" That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and even things you decided on a whim go smoothly.

ESTJ>ISTJ.title: Someone who explains things to the group, then works alone.
ESTJ>ISTJ.body: Once you've explained the steps to everyone, you quietly carry on alone. You check the facts, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. Some days you bring people together, and some days you want to work without talking to anyone. At work, you usually finish your own part early.
ESTJ>ISTJ.say: "That's all the steps. If there are no questions, I'll get started."
ESTJ>ISTJ.do: On moving day, you hand out tasks to your family and quietly sort the bookshelf alone.
ESTJ>ISTJ.worry: You think it's faster to do it yourself, so you take on too much. When you spend day after day with people, you can't shake off tiredness without alone time.
ESTJ>ISTJ.karai: "It's faster to do it myself than ask someone" has become your catchphrase.
ESTJ>ISTJ.aru: At the work party you happily run things till the end, but on your day off the next day, you don't want to set foot outside.
ESTJ>ISTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. That's why, after explaining things to everyone, you want to work alone.
ESTJ>ISTJ.yure: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your giving-instructions-at-work self or your day-off self.
ESTJ>ISTJ.plus: You want to do it yourself because you want the work done properly. People trust work done by someone like that.
ESTJ>ISTJ.tip: When you hand off work, say how it should look when it's done: "Up to here, please." You'll feel safe letting go, so you won't take on too much.
ESTJ>ISTJ.hidden: Do you somehow get energy when talking in front of people? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and you can split up work you've been carrying alone and move forward together.

ESTJ>ISFJ.title: Someone who remembers what everyone in the family likes.
ESTJ>ISFJ.body: You prepare things carefully for your family and the people close to you. You check the facts and stick to a plan. You care about people's feelings and get your energy back with time alone. For a family memorial or birthday, you book a restaurant to match the number of guests and what they like.
ESTJ>ISFJ.say: "I gave Grandma the seat by the window."
ESTJ>ISFJ.do: You decide the family's cooking turns and tell everyone every Sunday.
ESTJ>ISFJ.worry: Even when there's something you should say, you think about the other person's feelings and can't say it. While looking after everyone, you put yourself last.
ESTJ>ISFJ.karai: You can name everyone's favorites instantly, but when asked yours, you're stuck.
ESTJ>ISFJ.aru: At a family gathering, even when there's something you should say, you see the person's face and swallow it: "Oh well." On the way home you think, "I should've said it."
ESTJ>ISFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people and decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone and decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. That's why, even while preparing everything smoothly, you think about how everyone feels.
ESTJ>ISFJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your deciding-at-work self or your looking-after-family self.
ESTJ>ISFJ.plus: You can't say it because you care about the relationship. Thanks to your preparing, family gatherings always go smoothly.
ESTJ>ISFJ.tip: When there's something you want to say, try saying it that same day, not on the way home: "Can I say one thing?" Even a few words will leave you feeling lighter.
ESTJ>ISFJ.hidden: In discussions, do you find yourself saying, "Then it's faster to do it this way"? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and you can explain hard things clearly.

ESTJ>ESTJ.title: Someone who naturally settles "who does what, by when."
ESTJ>ESTJ.body: When people do something together, you naturally decide the roles and deadlines. Being with people gives you energy, and you check the facts, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. At work and at home, people think, "Ask them and you'll know the plan."
ESTJ>ESTJ.do: For the year-end cleaning, you assign everyone in the family an area and say, "By lunchtime, okay?"
ESTJ>ESTJ.worry: You get irritated with people who are vague or don't keep promises. Some days you worry you're pulling everyone along your way too much.
ESTJ>ESTJ.karai: Even on days off, as soon as you wake up you decide the order of what to do today.
ESTJ>ESTJ.aru: On a trip with friends, you put the schedule together and send it to the group chat without being asked, and the night before you send the meeting time once more.
ESTJ>ESTJ.why: Your temperament and personality are the same combination. You get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan, and it shows on both sides. That's why your personality tends to show up clearly in your result.
ESTJ>ESTJ.yure: Your temperament and personality match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day you want to relax alone or you're tired, your answers may come out a little different.
ESTJ>ESTJ.plus: You get irritated because you want everyone to see it through together. When you're around, things finish on schedule.
ESTJ>ESTJ.tip: When asking someone for something, first ask them, "By when do you think you can do it?" A deadline they set themselves is easier for them to keep.
ESTJ>ESTJ.hidden: Do you feel relieved on days you spend quietly alone? Getting your energy back with time alone is something you can do, too. Make some alone time now and then, and you'll feel more at ease around people.

ESTJ>ESFJ.title: Someone who runs things tightly and looks out for each person.
ESTJ>ESFJ.body: When people do something together, you run it tightly and keep it on schedule. But you also think about how each person feels. Being with people gives you energy, and you check the facts and stick to a plan. Even when setting up tents for a sports day, you plan the spots so no one has to sit in the sun.
ESTJ>ESFJ.say: "The farewell party is 3,000 yen each. I've already ordered the flowers."
ESTJ>ESFJ.do: After fairly assigning work duties, you quietly take over for someone who looks unwell.
ESTJ>ESFJ.worry: You go back and forth between wanting people to follow the rules and wanting to be kind to them. Sometimes you take on other people's work and wear yourself out.
ESTJ>ESFJ.karai: You're strict about rules, but you're the softest on anyone in trouble.
ESTJ>ESFJ.aru: You almost picked the restaurant because "it's close to the station," but in the end you chose again because "she'd probably like this one."
ESTJ>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. That's why, after deciding firmly, you sometimes choose again with people's feelings in mind.
ESTJ>ESFJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Answer thinking about setting rules at work and you lean toward logic. Answer thinking about looking after friends or family and you lean toward feelings.
ESTJ>ESFJ.plus: You go back and forth because you care about both rules and people. With an organizer who's firm and kind, everyone feels at ease joining in.
ESTJ>ESFJ.tip: Before taking on someone else's work, ask yourself once, "Could I ask someone else to do this?" Things will still run without you carrying it all.
ESTJ>ESFJ.hidden: When choosing a place or splitting the bill, can you quickly decide, "This one's cheaper and closer"? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. When feelings make you hesitate, comparing this way makes it easier to decide.

ESTJ>ISTP.title: Someone who gives instructions, then goes to fix it themselves.
ESTJ>ISTP.body: You're good at giving instructions, but before you know it you're doing the work yourself. You check the facts and decide with logic. Some days you want to stick to the plan, and some days you want to figure it out on the spot. When the copier stops at work, you might be the first to go check it.
ESTJ>ISTP.say: "Well, if it breaks, we'll figure it out then."
ESTJ>ISTP.do: When assembling furniture, you read the manual, then switch to your own way halfway and finish faster.
ESTJ>ISTP.worry: When you keep leading people, you want time to work quietly alone. You want to keep to the plan, but sometimes you want to change it on the spot, and even you get confused.
ESTJ>ISTP.karai: When a friend says, "I heard this works," you can't help asking, "Where'd you hear that?"
ESTJ>ISTP.aru: After a meeting where you lead everyone, you suddenly go quiet and want to rush home and play games or cook alone.
ESTJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and decide with logic. That's why, after giving instructions, you want to go fix things yourself.
ESTJ>ISTP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your leading-at-work self or your making-something-alone-on-a-day-off self.
ESTJ>ISTP.plus: You go fix things yourself because you notice trouble right away. With someone who can give instructions and use their hands, the work doesn't stop.
ESTJ>ISTP.tip: On days you're in charge, choose one person you can tell, "Call me if anything comes up." Even if you go fix something, the whole thing keeps going.
ESTJ>ISTP.hidden: When you start something, do you naturally set up the steps? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can carry the fixes you came up with on the spot over to next time.

ESTJ>ISFP.title: Someone who's very organized, but can't resist cute things.
ESTJ>ISFP.body: At work you're precise, yet on days off you take your time caring for favorite dishes and plants. People find it surprising, but valuing real facts and how things feel is a trait your temperament and your character share. You can move in a group or savor time alone, decide with logic or choose by feeling, plan ahead or follow your mood. That careful touch shows up everywhere.
ESTJ>ISFP.say: "Oh, this cup is such a nice color."
ESTJ>ISFP.do: You tidy your room fast, but you just can't decide where to put your decorations.
ESTJ>ISFP.worry: Quick decisions and slow, feeling moments swap places all day, and switching wears you out. Even with things you love, you think "I have to do this right," and some of the fun slips away.
ESTJ>ISFP.karai: When picking a place to eat, the first thing you check is the star rating.
ESTJ>ISFP.aru: Café hopping is supposed to be just for fun, but you catch yourself counting: "That's the fifth one this month."
ESTJ>ISFP.why: Your inborn temperament works among people, decides by logic, and follows a plan. Through experience, you grew the power to rest your heart alone, treasure what you love, and go with the mood of the moment. Relying on facts and things you can touch is the steady part shared by both. Switching wears you out, and that's proof you're really using both strengths.
ESTJ>ISFP.yure: Answer as your weekday office self or your weekend hobby self, and you might get almost completely different results. Three directions can wobble, so your result may change a lot each time.
ESTJ>ISFP.plus: You feel you have to do even your hobbies "properly" because you take everything seriously. With the power to feel and the power to get things done, your daily life slowly becomes more beautiful.
ESTJ>ISFP.tip: A few times a month, enjoy your hobby without counting how many or how long. When there are days you don't grade yourself, your hobby can truly be a rest.
ESTJ>ISFP.hidden: You treasure what you love, and the temperament you were born with can also think things through logically. When you rearrange your room and consider not just looks but "cleaning is easier if it goes here," that's this power. Use it on purpose, and if you turn something you love into work or a side job, you can shape it so it lasts.

ESTJ>ESTP.title: Someone who makes solid plans, then changes them on the day.
ESTJ>ESTP.body: You make proper plans, but on the day you go with the flow. Being with people gives you energy, and you check the facts and decide with logic. When something happens, you can quickly think of the next move. If it starts raining at a barbecue, you're right on it: "Let's move under the roof."
ESTJ>ESTP.say: "This is the plan. But if it rains, we'll change it on the spot."
ESTJ>ESTP.do: When a friend invites you to golf, you're at the driving range by the next weekend.
ESTJ>ESTP.worry: You want to keep to your plans, but you also want to change them on the spot, and you worry you're jerking people around. You're not good at sitting still, so even on days off you want to do something.
ESTJ>ESTP.karai: You're fast at making plans, and even faster at changing them.
ESTJ>ESTP.aru: You researched your trip carefully, but once you get there you say, "This looks more fun," and change several plans.
ESTJ>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type to stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and decide with logic. That's why, even after making plans, you want to change them on the spot.
ESTJ>ESTP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a work deadline and you answer like a planner. Picture heading out for fun and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ESTJ>ESTP.plus: You want to change things on the spot because you quickly notice a better way. With someone who can plan and move fast, everyone feels safe when something comes up.
ESTJ>ESTP.tip: When you change plans, tell everyone, "I'm just changing this part." Then they can follow along with peace of mind.
ESTJ>ESTP.hidden: Do you get up at the same time every morning and get ready in the same order? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, even when you change plans on the spot, you don't drop the important things.

ESTJ>ESFP.title: Someone who prepares carefully, then has the most fun on the day.
ESTJ>ESFP.body: You take charge of getting things ready, and on the day you have the most fun. Being with people gives you energy, and you care about what's in front of you. You think about everyone's feelings and brighten up the room. Even on trips, you're the one who says, "Let's stop here," between plans.
ESTJ>ESFP.say: "When we're done cleaning up, let's all have ice cream."
ESTJ>ESFP.do: During big cleanups, you put on music and get everyone going while you tidy up quickly.
ESTJ>ESFP.worry: You want everyone to have fun so much that you sometimes don't notice you're tired. Some days you go back and forth between wanting to do things properly and wanting to go with the mood.
ESTJ>ESFP.karai: While you're deciding the karaoke order, you run out of time to sing yourself.
ESTJ>ESFP.aru: At a birthday party, you run everything from setup to the program, but when the cake comes out, you're singing the loudest.
ESTJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with logic and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with your feelings and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people and trust facts and experience. That's why, after preparing carefully, you can enjoy the day on a whim.
ESTJ>ESFP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer as your preparing-at-work self and the result comes out structured. Answer as your hanging-out-with-friends self and it comes out softer.
ESTJ>ESFP.plus: You don't notice your tiredness because you're happy when everyone's having fun. With someone who prepares and has the most fun too, the whole room lights up.
ESTJ>ESFP.tip: When you're asked to prepare for a get-together, hand just one task to someone else. You'll still have time to enjoy yourself.
ESTJ>ESFP.hidden: When choosing a place, do you quickly compare, "Which is cheaper?" That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and fun plans can move forward without strain.

ESFJ>INTJ.title: Someone who finds the fastest way and helps until you get used to it.
ESFJ>INTJ.body: You figure out the fastest way to get things done and stick to a plan. But you also keep an eye on whether anyone's struggling. You want time to think things through alone, too. When a new way of working is decided, you might stay by someone who isn't used to it yet and show them how.
ESFJ>INTJ.say: "This way is fastest. I'll help until you get the hang of it."
ESFJ>INTJ.do: You plan the family trip alone and fit in one place each person wants to visit.
ESFJ>INTJ.worry: Some days you want to think alone, and some days you want to look after everyone, and you can't decide which. After deciding firmly, you worry you came across as cold.
ESFJ>INTJ.karai: The day before meeting up, you send the time to the group chat once more, just in case.
ESFJ>INTJ.aru: You turned down a friend's invite and spent the day thinking alone. It was relaxing, but at night you feel a little guilty.
ESFJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone, follow your ideas, and decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you stick to a plan. That's why, after deciding on the fastest way, you think about everyone.
ESFJ>INTJ.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your planning-alone self or your looking-after-everyone self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>INTJ.plus: You worry you seemed cold because you care about people. Someone who teaches the fast way and helps until others get used to it is someone people rely on.
ESFJ>INTJ.tip: On days you turn down invites to be alone, decide first: "Today's a rest day." You can relax without feeling guilty.
ESFJ>INTJ.hidden: When you go to a gathering, do you get more energy than you expected? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Plans you made alone get even better when you talk them over with others.

ESFJ>INTP.title: Someone who thinks things through, then answers with others in mind.
ESFJ>INTP.body: You think things through carefully and come up with answers that make sense. But you also worry whether your answer will cause trouble for anyone. In this combination, all four parts of your temperament and personality are flipped. Some days you want to think alone, and some days you want to talk with people. When a family member can't figure out how to use an appliance, you think of an easy way to explain it.
ESFJ>INTP.say: "That makes sense. But would anyone have trouble with it?"
ESFJ>INTP.do: When you hear people's schedules don't match, you quietly find a day everyone can make and send it.
ESFJ>INTP.worry: After being honest, you worry you hurt the other person. Sometimes you go back and forth between wanting to think alone and wanting to go along with everyone.
ESFJ>INTP.karai: You're the one who keeps worrying the longest about the thing you said you "don't really mind."
ESFJ>INTP.aru: After giving a friend your honest opinion when they asked for advice, you worry, "Did I hurt them?" and keep thinking about it late into the night.
ESFJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone, follow your ideas, decide with logic, and go with the flow. All four parts are flipped in this combination. That's why, even when your answer makes sense, you worry about how people feel.
ESFJ>INTP.yure: All four parts are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Answering as your thinking-alone self or your chatting-with-friends self could give opposite results.
ESFJ>INTP.plus: You worry because you care about people. Someone who shares well-thought-out answers with the other person in mind is someone people trust.
ESFJ>INTP.tip: When you share an honest opinion, end by asking, "What do you think?" Knowing how they feel means you won't worry so much at night.
ESFJ>INTP.hidden: Do your thoughts come together while talking with people? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Try talking through what you thought about alone, and your answers will get even better.

ESFJ>ENTJ.title: Someone who sets clear goals and moves forward with everyone.
ESFJ>ENTJ.body: You set clear goals and lead everyone forward. Being with people gives you energy, and you make plans early. Some days you say tough things, but you also keep an eye on how everyone's doing. When it's someone's birthday on the team, you might quietly have a cake ready.
ESFJ>ENTJ.say: "Let's continue the goal talk over lunch together."
ESFJ>ENTJ.do: When planning a big project, you've already booked the restaurant for the wrap-up party.
ESFJ>ENTJ.worry: You want to decide clearly, but when someone seems unhappy, you can't. You go back and forth between putting the goal first and putting everyone's feelings first.
ESFJ>ENTJ.karai: You're strict about goals, but you take forever choosing snacks to bring for everyone.
ESFJ>ENTJ.aru: Even when something has to be decided in a meeting, if someone looks unhappy, you end up saying, "Let's pick this up next time."
ESFJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people and stick to a plan. That's why, even when you want to decide clearly, you can't help noticing how everyone looks.
ESFJ>ENTJ.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work goals and you lean toward ideas and logic. Picture time with your team and you lean toward facts and feelings.
ESFJ>ENTJ.plus: You can't decide because you care about everyone's feelings. People want to follow someone with clear goals who also watches out for them.
ESFJ>ENTJ.tip: When it's hard to decide, make the decision smaller: "Let's decide this much today and the rest next week." The talk keeps moving.
ESFJ>ENTJ.hidden: Do you notice small changes in your teammates and ask, "How've you been?" That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and even with tough goals, everyone can work without pushing too hard.

ESFJ>ENTP.title: Someone who puts people at ease and comes up with unexpected ideas.
ESFJ>ENTP.body: You love talking with people, and while talking you come up with unexpected ideas. You soften the mood so everyone can speak easily. When deciding, you often think it through with logic. When a meeting stalls, you might change the flow by saying, "Can I go off-topic for a sec?"
ESFJ>ENTP.say: "What if we look at that problem from the other way around?"
ESFJ>ENTP.do: When helping at the neighborhood festival, you chat with everyone who comes while working the front desk.
ESFJ>ENTP.worry: When the conversation gets lively, you end up saying too much and regret it later. You go back and forth between keeping the usual way and trying a new one.
ESFJ>ENTP.karai: Even for a dish where you were told "plain is fine," you can't help adding a little twist.
ESFJ>ENTP.aru: You were listening to a friend's problem, but halfway through the discussion itself becomes fun, and on the way home you reflect, "I may have said too much."
ESFJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas, decide with logic, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people. That's why new ideas come out while you're talking with people.
ESFJ>ENTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your debating-with-friends self or your looking-after-family self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>ENTP.plus: You can reflect on saying too much because you think about the other person's feelings. Someone who makes it easy to talk and also brings new ideas is welcome anywhere.
ESFJ>ENTP.tip: When the talk heats up, pause and ask, "By the way, what do you think?" You'll know how they feel before you say too much.
ESFJ>ENTP.hidden: Do you remember what your friends like and what they told you before? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can shape new ideas to fit the person.

ESFJ>INFJ.title: Someone who really cheers on a friend's job change or move.
ESFJ>INFJ.body: When a friend is struggling, you think with them about what's next for them. You care about people's feelings and set plans early. You like lively places, but you also want quiet time to think alone. When you hear a friend is moving, you might look up good restaurants in their new town.
ESFJ>INFJ.say: "I'm sure there's a workplace that suits you better."
ESFJ>INFJ.do: When a friend asks for advice about changing jobs, you look for good openings and send them.
ESFJ>INFJ.worry: You think about other people's worries as if they were your own, and it wears you out. After a lively time, you're confused by how suddenly you want to be alone.
ESFJ>INFJ.karai: Even before the trip destination is decided, you're already looking up places everyone would love.
ESFJ>INFJ.aru: You love lively dinners with friends and enjoy them to the end, but the moment you get home, you suddenly want to be alone.
ESFJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people and trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone and follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with your feelings and stick to a plan. That's why you want to think about a friend's future too.
ESFJ>INFJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your having-dinner-with-friends self or your thinking-alone-at-home self.
ESFJ>INFJ.plus: It wears you out because you truly think about the other person. Having a friend who thinks things through with you that much is reassuring.
ESFJ>INFJ.tip: On days you've listened to someone's worries, put your phone down when you get home and take a long bath. You'll reset and be ready to listen again the next day.
ESFJ>INFJ.hidden: Do you feel your energy rising as you talk with friends? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and instead of worrying alone, you can find answers by talking with others.

ESFJ>INFP.title: Someone who loves looking after people and values time alone too.
ESFJ>INFP.body: You often look after the people around you. Caring about people's feelings never changes for you. But you also really value time alone doing what you love. On a day-off evening, you might be watching a favorite movie with a cup of tea.
ESFJ>INFP.say: "You can keep eating, but there's something I'd like to talk to you about."
ESFJ>INFP.do: After taking care of family errands, you spend the night relaxing alone with your favorite music.
ESFJ>INFP.worry: You can ask what others want to do, but you can't bring up what you want. When you've been going along with everyone for a while, you want to be alone.
ESFJ>INFP.karai: You tell others, "Do whatever you like," but you can't say it to yourself.
ESFJ>INFP.aru: You go around asking everyone, "What do you want to do?" but you can hardly bring up what you want to do.
ESFJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone, follow your ideas, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with your feelings. That's why, after looking after people, you want to do what you love alone.
ESFJ>INFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your looking-after-family-and-friends self or your doing-what-you-love-alone self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>INFP.plus: You can't bring it up because you think about everyone's feelings first. When someone like you says, "I want to do this," the people around you will surely cheer you on.
ESFJ>INFP.tip: Once a week, tell someone you trust one thing you want to do. Saying it out loud helps you start doing it, little by little.
ESFJ>INFP.hidden: Do you settle the date and place for get-togethers early? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can put what you want to do on your schedule and make it happen.

ESFJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who takes on the yearly events and makes them better.
ESFJ>ENFJ.body: You take on events where everyone gathers and make them a little better each year. Being with people gives you energy, you care about people's feelings, and you set plans early. For the neighborhood summer festival, you might use what you learned last year and add one game for the kids.
ESFJ>ENFJ.say: "If it's okay with everyone, I'll be on the committee this year."
ESFJ>ENFJ.do: When a younger coworker is handed their first task, you keep an eye on them until it's done and ask, "How's it going?" a few times.
ESFJ>ENFJ.worry: While doing things for everyone, you don't notice you're overdoing it. Sometimes you can't decide whether to keep the usual way or add something new.
ESFJ>ENFJ.karai: "Don't overdo it" is your catchphrase, but you're the one overdoing it the most.
ESFJ>ENFJ.aru: You run the yearly event exactly like last year. On the way home after it's over, you're already saying, "Next year, let's try this too."
ESFJ>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. That's why, after running things like last year, you start thinking about next year.
ESFJ>ENFJ.yure: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. Picture preparing for a yearly event and you lean toward facts. Picture what you want to do from now on and you lean toward ideas.
ESFJ>ENFJ.plus: You overdo it because you want everyone to be happy. With someone who takes on events and makes them better every year, the neighborhood or the team gets livelier.
ESFJ>ENFJ.tip: When you take on a role, ask someone for help with just one thing at the start: "Could you take care of this part?" You won't have to push yourself alone.
ESFJ>ENFJ.hidden: Do you remember how things went before, like "Last year it was like this"? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Because of it, even when you add something new, the event still runs smoothly.

ESFJ>ENFP.title: Someone who books the usual place, then invites you to a new one next.
ESFJ>ENFP.body: You love being with people, and when you find something fun, you invite others right away. You care about people's feelings and make sure everyone's having fun. You value the usual ways, but new things catch your interest quickly too. When you meet friends on a day off, the topics keep changing and suddenly it's evening.
ESFJ>ENFP.say: "I love your haircut! Where'd you get it done?"
ESFJ>ENFP.do: For family birthdays, you come up with a different surprise every year.
ESFJ>ENFP.worry: There are so many fun things that you pack your schedule too full and get tired. Some days you can't decide between the usual way and something new.
ESFJ>ENFP.karai: You're careful with reservations and payments, but picking an outfit takes you the longest.
ESFJ>ENFP.aru: You book the usual place for lunch with friends, but on the way home you're already saying, "Next time, that new café."
ESFJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people and decide with your feelings. That's why you love your usual place but also want to try new ones.
ESFJ>ENFP.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture preparing for yearly events and you answer in a structured way. Picture hanging out with friends and you answer more freely.
ESFJ>ENFP.plus: You overpack your schedule because you love spending time with people. Because you invite everyone, there are more fun plans for all.
ESFJ>ENFP.tip: When making plans, set one "nothing" day each week first. You won't get worn out, and you can look forward to the next fun thing.
ESFJ>ENFP.hidden: Do you always take care of reservations and payments properly? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, even when you invite people on a whim, everyone can come with peace of mind.

ESFJ>ISTJ.title: Someone who's accurate at work and quick to check on people in trouble.
ESFJ>ISTJ.body: You do your work accurately, by the rules. You check the facts and stick to a plan. But when someone nearby is having a hard time, you notice right away and talk to them. You like talking with people, but you also value time to work quietly alone. On a rainy day, you might lend your spare umbrella to a coworker who doesn't have one.
ESFJ>ISTJ.say: "The paperwork is fine. More importantly, you look pale. Are you sleeping?"
ESFJ>ISTJ.do: After doing your expense report by the rules, you quietly leave a throat lozenge on a coworker's desk.
ESFJ>ISTJ.worry: Some days you're torn between following the rules and helping people, and you can't decide. When you've been talking with people day after day, you want some quiet time alone.
ESFJ>ISTJ.karai: For the work party, you book the place everyone liked last time again.
ESFJ>ISTJ.aru: On days you're torn between following the rules and helping someone in trouble right in front of you, you keep thinking about it even after you get home.
ESFJ>ISTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people and decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone and decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. That's why, even while working accurately, you can't stop thinking about people in trouble.
ESFJ>ISTJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your working-alone self or your chatting-with-coworkers self.
ESFJ>ISTJ.plus: You're torn because you care about both rules and people. Someone who works accurately and checks on people in trouble is trusted at work.
ESFJ>ISTJ.tip: Decide the order ahead of time: "First do it by the rules, then look for ways to help." You won't keep thinking about it after you get home.
ESFJ>ISTJ.hidden: Does chatting with coworkers brighten your mood? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and it'll be easier to talk to someone about work you've been carrying alone.

ESFJ>ISFJ.title: Someone who moves first so everyone can have a good time.
ESFJ>ISFJ.body: You move first and prepare so everyone can have a good time. You care about people's feelings, check the facts, and stick to a plan. Sometimes you're in front of people, but you also like quiet time preparing alone. On days you have guests over, you've lined up the right number of slippers the day before.
ESFJ>ISFJ.say: "If anyone's cold, I've got lap blankets ready."
ESFJ>ISFJ.do: When you hear a friend is in the hospital, you go visit right away with a magazine and drink they'd like.
ESFJ>ISFJ.worry: While going along with everyone, your own plans and feelings get put last. After a day of working hard in front of people, you don't get your energy back until you relax alone.
ESFJ>ISFJ.karai: While matching everyone's schedules, your own always ends up last.
ESFJ>ISFJ.aru: You cheerfully emcee the welcome party, but you've actually asked the new hires ahead of time what they can't eat and quietly had the dishes changed.
ESFJ>ISFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. That's why you can look out for everyone, both up front and behind the scenes.
ESFJ>ISFJ.yure: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your emcee-or-organizer self or your preparing-alone-at-home self.
ESFJ>ISFJ.plus: You put yourself last because you think about everyone's feelings first. Thanks to your preparing, get-togethers always go smoothly.
ESFJ>ISFJ.tip: Before matching everyone's schedules, tell them the days you can't make first. Your own plans will be protected too.
ESFJ>ISFJ.hidden: Does your mood brighten as you talk with people? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and you can share what you prepared behind the scenes in a fun way with everyone.

ESFJ>ESTJ.title: Someone who wraps up discussions and checks in with each person after.
ESFJ>ESTJ.body: You wrap up discussions quickly and decide on time. Being with people gives you energy, and you check the facts and stick to a plan. After deciding, you also make sure to think about how each person feels. After assigning roles in a club, you might tell someone who didn't get their choice, "You'll get first pick next time."
ESFJ>ESTJ.say: "We'll go with this plan. Does anyone have anything left to say?"
ESFJ>ESTJ.do: You fairly split the family chores, then take over for whoever's tired: "Just for today."
ESFJ>ESTJ.worry: After being direct, you worry you said it too harshly. You go back and forth between wanting people to follow the rules and wanting to be kind to them.
ESFJ>ESTJ.karai: After strictly pointing something out, you quietly leave the person's favorite snack on their desk.
ESFJ>ESTJ.aru: You said what was right, but when the other person goes quiet, you spend the whole night wondering, "Did I say it the wrong way?"
ESFJ>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. That's why, after deciding clearly, you worry about the other person's feelings.
ESFJ>ESTJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Answer thinking about making decisions in a meeting and you lean toward logic. Think of family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ESFJ>ESTJ.plus: You worry about how you said it because you care about the person. With someone who decides properly and checks in afterward in charge, everyone feels at ease.
ESFJ>ESTJ.tip: When pointing something out, start by saying, "I just have one request." The other person can get ready to listen and is less likely to go quiet.
ESFJ>ESTJ.hidden: When someone's down, do you notice right away and go to them? That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and even when saying hard things, you can say them in a way that gets through.

ESFJ>ESFJ.title: Someone who looks out for the people around them wherever they are.
ESFJ>ESFJ.body: Wherever you are, you keep an eye on whether the people around you are having a good time. Being with people gives you energy, and you care about feelings, check the facts, and stick to a plan. At work, you might invite someone new: "Want to grab lunch together?"
ESFJ>ESFJ.say: "There's more, so tell me if you need seconds."
ESFJ>ESFJ.do: You keep your friends' birthdays in your calendar and send a message every year.
ESFJ>ESFJ.worry: You worry about people's reactions, and small things bring you down. Some days you put everyone first so much that you lose track of what you want to do.
ESFJ>ESFJ.karai: You remember everyone's favorite drinks, but forget to order your own.
ESFJ>ESFJ.aru: When one person's reply in the group chat is short, you wonder, "Did I upset them?" and it bugs you all day.
ESFJ>ESFJ.why: Your temperament and personality are the same combination. You get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan, and it shows on both sides. That's why your kindness tends to show up just as it is in your result.
ESFJ>ESFJ.yure: Your temperament and personality match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day you're tired of people and want to be alone, your answers may come out a little different.
ESFJ>ESFJ.plus: You worry about people's reactions because you're sensitive to their feelings. When you're around, people feel cared for.
ESFJ>ESFJ.tip: If someone's reply is short, don't worry about it right away. Sleep on it. The next day, you'll usually find it was nothing.
ESFJ>ESFJ.hidden: Do you feel calm on days you spend relaxing alone? Getting your energy back with time alone is something you can do, too. Make some alone time now and then, and you won't worry so much about people's reactions.

ESFJ>ISTP.title: Someone who opens the toolbox before finding words.
ESFJ>ISTP.body: When someone's in trouble, you help by doing something before finding the words. You check the facts and care about what's in front of you. You like gatherings, but you also value time to work quietly alone. If a friend's shelf is wobbly, you tighten the screws without a word.
ESFJ>ISTP.say: "Let me see that. I think it can be fixed right here."
ESFJ>ISTP.do: At family gatherings, you end up fixing the glitchy TV or Wi-Fi alone.
ESFJ>ISTP.worry: You're not good at putting feelings into words, so when you want to comfort someone, you can't find what to say. Some days you want to stick to the plan, and some days you want to act on the spot, and even you get confused.
ESFJ>ISTP.karai: When someone thanks you, you get shy and say quickly, "Oh, it was just luck."
ESFJ>ISTP.aru: When a friend is down, you can't find the right words, so for now you buy their favorite snack and hand it to them.
ESFJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone, decide with logic, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience. That's why your hands move before words of comfort do.
ESFJ>ISTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your fixing-something-alone self or your looking-after-everyone-at-a-gathering self can give totally different results.
ESFJ>ISTP.plus: You can't find the words because your body moves before your mouth. The kindness of quietly fixing things or handing over a favorite snack really does come across.
ESFJ>ISTP.tip: After fixing something for someone, add just, "Let me know if anything else comes up." Even with few words, your feelings get through.
ESFJ>ISTP.hidden: Do you notice right away when someone's feeling low? That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and you can not only help with your hands but also just be there for them.

ESFJ>ISFP.title: Someone who looks after everyone, then takes a break alone.
ESFJ>ISFP.body: You often look after the people around you. You care about people's feelings, what's in front of you, and pretty things. After time with people, you take a break alone, listening to your favorite music or drinking tea. When you go shopping, you might end up buying one cute plate that wasn't on the plan.
ESFJ>ISFP.say: "I love this dish. The color is so gentle."
ESFJ>ISFP.do: When having friends over, you plan the menu ahead, but pick the table flowers on the day by mood.
ESFJ>ISFP.worry: You fill your schedule with plans for others and can't make time for yourself. Some days you want to stick to the plan, and some days you want to follow your mood, and you can't decide.
ESFJ>ISFP.karai: Your plans for others are packed, and your plans for yourself are "if I feel like it."
ESFJ>ISFP.aru: After having friends over and looking after everyone, you make tea with a scent you love and quietly slip back into your own time.
ESFJ>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type to get energy from being with people and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to recharge with time alone and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and decide with your feelings. That's why, after looking after everyone, you want to rest alone.
ESFJ>ISFP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your hosting-friends self or your relaxing-alone self.
ESFJ>ISFP.plus: You can't make time for yourself because you love doing things for others. The time you prepare for everyone is comfortable for all.
ESFJ>ISFP.tip: Put just one plan for yourself in your calendar first. It'll give you real rest, better than "if I feel like it."
ESFJ>ISFP.hidden: Do you naturally get energy when everyone gathers? That's your temperament, which gets energy from people. Use it, and you can share the things you enjoy alone with others too.

ESFJ>ESTP.title: Someone who asks "Are you okay?" and then moves fast.
ESFJ>ESTP.body: When something happens, you look out for people and act right away. Being with people gives you energy, and you care about the facts in front of you. When deciding, you decide quickly on the spot. If you forget gear while camping, you look up a nearby store right away and somehow make it work.
ESFJ>ESTP.say: "The trains are stopped? Then let's take a taxi."
ESFJ>ESTP.do: When you learn it'll rain on the day of an event, you switch to the rainy-day plan right away.
ESFJ>ESTP.worry: Sometimes you move so fast that you push ahead before asking how the other person feels. You want to keep to your plans, but sometimes you want to change them on the spot.
ESFJ>ESTP.karai: While worrying about everyone, you're secretly itching to move on to the next thing.
ESFJ>ESTP.aru: When a lost friend calls you, before asking how they feel, you jump into action: "Where are you? Send me a map."
ESFJ>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with your feelings and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with logic and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people and trust facts and experience. That's why, after checking on people, you can move on to the next step right away.
ESFJ>ESTP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer as your handling-trouble self and you lean toward logic and the moment. Answer as your listening-to-a-friend self and you lean toward feelings and planning.
ESFJ>ESTP.plus: You move fast because you want to help people in trouble quickly. It's reassuring to have someone who acts first when something happens.
ESFJ>ESTP.tip: When someone's in trouble, after "Are you okay?" add, "What would you like to do?" before acting. You can help in a way that fits how they feel.
ESFJ>ESTP.hidden: Do you get your plans and things ready by the day before? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, you can act calmly even when something sudden comes up.

ESFJ>ESFP.title: Someone who books early, then enjoys detours on the day.
ESFJ>ESFP.body: You prepare properly ahead of time, and on the day you enjoy every moment. Being with people gives you energy, and you care about people's feelings and what's in front of you. When everyone's having fun, you're happy too. On a trip, when you find a place that looks tasty, you might say, "Let's try it," even if it's not on the plan.
ESFJ>ESFP.say: "How's this outfit? I wore it because I wanted to show everyone!"
ESFJ>ESFP.do: At your kid's sports day, you prepare the lunch properly and you're the loudest one cheering.
ESFJ>ESFP.worry: Sometimes you're having so much fun that you stay longer than planned. Some days you go back and forth between sticking to the plan and enjoying the moment.
ESFJ>ESFP.karai: On the very day you say, "I'm leaving early today," you stay till the end.
ESFJ>ESFP.aru: You booked the restaurant for six, but before that you say, "Let's stop by the crepe stand for a bit."
ESFJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type to stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you get energy from being with people, trust facts and experience, and decide with your feelings. That's why, even after booking properly, you want to take detours on the day.
ESFJ>ESFP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture preparing for an event and you answer like a planner. Picture heading out for fun and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ESFJ>ESFP.plus: You stay longer because you love spending time with everyone. With someone who prepares properly and has the most fun on the day, the room lights up.
ESFJ>ESFP.tip: On days out, decide just one thing: "I'll head home at this time." Until then, you can fully enjoy your detours.
ESFJ>ESFP.hidden: Do you take care of reservations and what to bring ahead of time? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, everyone can take detours with peace of mind on the day.
